summary:
ASTRIS: Onboard Crew Health Monitoring and Triage System

ASTRIS is a health monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during space missions, especially when communication with Earth is limited. In space, astronauts may face health issues that need immediate attention, so having a reliable onboard health system is important.

Our project provides a single platform where crew members can enter and monitor their vital signs, such as heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, blood pressure and glucose levels. Its main innovation is ASTRA AI, an intelligent health assistant that analyses the entered health data, identifies possible health risks and provides quick guidance on what to do next.

ASTRIS also includes features such as health history tracking, body system monitoring, triage levels, check-up scheduling, response logs and printable medical reports. It also provides information about solar radiation using NASA's space-weather data.

Our aim is to make health monitoring easier and help astronauts respond to possible medical emergencies, even without continuous support from Earth.
details:
ASTRIS & ASTRA [Autonomous Space Telemetry & Response Assistant]

An Offline-First Astronaut Health Monitoring and Triage System

1. Project Overview

Our Team ASTRIS presents ASTRA (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Response Assistant) which is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and triage platform designed to support crew members during space missions, particularly missions to the Moon and Mars.

During long-duration space missions, astronauts may experience health-related problems due to isolation, radiation exposure, changes in their environment and limited access to immediate medical assistance. Communication delays between Earth and distant space missions can also make it difficult to receive timely medical guidance.

ASTRIS aims to address this challenge by providing an onboard platform that helps astronauts monitor their health, identify unusual changes in vital signs and receive immediate guidance without depending on continuous communication with Earth.

The platform combines health monitoring, rule-based analysis, an intelligent assistant, medical response logging and environmental information in one dashboard.

2. Our Main Innovation – ASTRA AI

The most important innovation of our project is ASTRA AI (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Response Assistant), an intelligent onboard health assistant designed specifically for astronaut healthcare.

ASTRA helps astronauts understand their health condition by analyzing the readings entered into ASTRIS. It can answer questions about health parameters, explain active alerts, identify the current triage status and provide guidance on the next steps.

Unlike a system that depends entirely on cloud-based AI services, ASTRA is designed to work using information available on the device itself. This makes it useful in situations where communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

ASTRA includes quick actions such as:

  • Checking the astronaut's current health status.
  • Explaining the reason behind a particular triage level.
  • Identifying active health alerts.
  • Providing information about individual vital signs.
  • Explaining how to measure parameters such as SpO₂.
  • Suggesting the next health check.
  • Explaining how the analysis model works.

ASTRA currently uses a rule-based approach rather than a medically validated AI diagnostic model. Its purpose is to provide understandable triage guidance, not to replace doctors or flight surgeons.

3. Website Features and Functionality

Our website is designed as a central control dashboard where astronauts can access all the health monitoring and response features.

A. Overview Dashboard

The overview page provides a quick summary of the crew member's health status. It displays the current triage level, available health readings, alerts and check-up schedule. It also provides shortcuts to save a check-in, ask ASTRA, contact a medical officer and generate a handover report.

B. Crew Member Management

The platform allows users to create, select, rename and remove crew member profiles. This makes it possible to maintain separate health records for different astronauts.

C. Health Monitoring and Check-ins

Astronauts can manually enter or update their health readings. The system supports important parameters such as:

  • Heart rate
  • Blood oxygen level (SpO₂)
  • Body temperature
  • Systolic blood pressure
  • Blood glucose
  • Sleep and mood information

The readings are saved as check-ins, allowing the system to maintain a history of health information. Sample normal and emergency drill readings are also available for demonstration.

D. Triage and Alert System

This feature evaluates the entered readings and identifies possible health concerns. It uses different levels of response, including normal monitoring, rechecking readings and escalation when necessary.

The system explains why a particular triage level has been assigned and highlights readings that require attention. This helps astronauts understand when they should recheck a measurement or seek medical assistance.

E. ASTRA AI Assistant

ASTRA acts as the onboard health assistant. Users can interact with it through a chat interface and ask questions about their readings, alerts and recommended next steps. It uses the available health data on the device to provide contextual guidance.

F. Body Systems Map

The body systems section provides a visual representation of different body systems and their monitoring status. It helps users identify which systems may require attention.

It uses status indicators such as Normal, Recheck, Escalate, Check Sensor and No Data to make health information easier to understand.

G. Model Analysis and Evaluation

This section explains how the health analysis system works. It considers reference ranges, unusual readings, personal baselines and changes in readings over time.

The website also provides options to:

  • Add simulated health history.
  • Import baseline reference data.
  • Run model benchmarks.
  • View per-measure statistics.
  • Evaluate how the model responds to different sample readings.

The system uses simulated data for demonstration and testing. It does not claim to have been validated using actual astronaut medical records.

H. Health History and Trend Analysis

ASTRIS stores previous check-ins and allows users to view changes in their health readings over time. Trend graphs display the last 12 saved values for a selected parameter.

This helps identify repeated unusual readings or gradual changes that might otherwise go unnoticed.

I. Check-up Scheduling

The check schedule feature allows users to set intervals for regular health check-ins. The system keeps track of missed checks and includes an escalation window following a critical check-in.

This encourages regular monitoring rather than waiting until a health problem becomes serious.

J. Response Log and Medical Handover

The response log records actions such as saved check-ins, acknowledgements, rechecks and medical officer contacts.

Users can also generate printable handover reports containing relevant information that can assist in communicating the astronaut's health status to medical personnel.

These records help maintain a history of actions taken during a health-related event.

K. Solar Radiation Monitoring

Space radiation is an important environmental risk for astronauts. ASTRIS includes a solar radiation section that connects with NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information).

It allows users to check available solar flare and space-weather information, helping them remain aware of potential radiation-related environmental events.

ASTRIS does not directly measure radiation dose. Actual radiation monitoring requires appropriate onboard dosimeters.

L. Data Import and Export

The platform supports importing and exporting health records in CSV and JSON formats. This makes it easier to maintain, transfer and analyze health information when required.

The records and response logs are stored locally on the device, supporting the platform's offline-first approach.

4. How the System Works

The basic working process of ASTRIS can be explained in five steps:

  1. Data Entry: The astronaut enters health readings through the website.
  2. Data Analysis: The system compares readings with expected reference ranges and available personal health baselines.
  3. Risk Identification: Unusual readings, repeated changes and possible sensor errors are identified.
  4. Triage and Guidance: The system determines an appropriate triage level and ASTRA provides understandable guidance.
  5. Record Keeping: The check-in, alerts and actions taken are stored in the health history and response log.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend Development: HTML for building the website structure and user interface.
  • Deployment: Vercel for hosting and making the website accessible online.
  • Data Management: CSV and JSON formats for importing and exporting health records.
  • NASA Data Source: NASA DONKI API for accessing solar flare and space-weather information.
  • Hardware: Currently a software-based prototype. Bluetooth wearable sensors are planned for future integration.

5. What Makes ASTRIS Different?

The main strength of ASTRIS is that it brings several important functions together in a single onboard platform.

Instead of having separate systems for health readings, alerts, medical guidance and record keeping, ASTRIS combines them into one interface.

Its offline-first design reduces dependence on continuous communication with Earth. Its personal baseline and trend analysis features also help identify changes rather than looking at individual readings alone.

The integration of ASTRA, health triage, response logging and NASA space-weather information makes it a useful prototype for exploring the future of astronaut healthcare.

6. Future Scope

Although the current version is a functional website prototype, several improvements can make ASTRIS more suitable for actual space missions.

  • Wearable Sensor Integration: Connecting Bluetooth-enabled devices to automatically collect heart rate, SpO₂, skin temperature and other available health readings.
  • Real-Time Monitoring: Continuously monitoring astronaut health without requiring manual data entry.
  • Advanced AI Models: Developing more advanced predictive models using validated medical datasets.
  • Radiation Sensor Integration: Connecting appropriate radiation monitoring hardware to track actual radiation exposure.
  • Improved Medical Support: Developing better communication and reporting systems for astronauts and medical officers.
  • Mission-Specific Customization: Adapting the platform to the requirements of future Moon and Mars missions.

7. Expected Impact

ASTRIS aims to improve how astronaut health information is monitored and managed during space exploration. By combining continuous monitoring as a future goal, early identification of unusual readings, triage guidance and organized medical records, the system can help astronauts respond more effectively to potential health concerns.

It is particularly relevant to long-duration missions where communication delays and limited medical resources make onboard health support important.

8. Conclusion

ASTRIS is our attempt to address one of the important challenges of future space exploration: keeping astronauts healthy and safe when immediate medical support from Earth may not be available.

Through its health monitoring dashboard, ASTRA intelligent assistant, triage system, trend analysis and space-weather monitoring, ASTRIS provides a unified approach to astronaut health management.

Our vision is to develop ASTRIS into a reliable onboard health support platform that helps astronauts make informed decisions and supports safer missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond.
